attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, which he endorses.

semantics.note: This is a firm claim that a trend is under way. The wording matches the source. No metric is named.

contract.note: The plain reading (more substitution, narrower differences, competition on price) is fair and ordinary. Limiting it to June 1–25 is narrow, because he presents this as a long-running view. Here the window does not change the result.

evidence.note: OpenRouter's own disclosure about cheaper open-weight substitutes for some workloads. It also describes a steady 3–6 month capability gap rather than a narrowing one. It has no market-wide trend series.
The same report notes ongoing differences in deployment, modality and licensing. That qualifies the substitution story but does not disprove a trend toward commoditization.

reviews.rationale: The only source is one company blog. It shows cheaper substitutes in some workloads, but the packet has no dated comparisons of substitution, switching or narrowing capability across the market. The contract asks for exactly that evidence, so the claim cannot be settled.

attribution.note: These are Marcus's own figures, written in his own post.

semantics.note: All six figures are kept with their qualifiers. SoftBank's figure correctly has no period attached.

contract.note: Comparing closes from May 26 to June 26 is an ordinary reading, and the contract allows for differences in when prices were captured. The SoftBank result depends on reading the period as monthly or daily, and the speaker gave no period.

evidence.note: Nvidia is down about 10.4% from close to close, which meets 'over 8%'. The May 26 row is cut off in the excerpt, but every nearby baseline also exceeds 8%.
Oracle is down 23.07% at the close. Its June 26 trading range allows about 22%, so this is roughly consistent but not exact.
CoreWeave is down 8.79% at the close, and still down 7.37% at the June 26 high. 'A bit over 4%' is clearly wrong.
SoftBank is down 20.6% for the month but 12.53% for the day. The daily figure matches the unanchored 'about 12%'; the monthly reading would contradict it.
Cerebras is down 24.87% at the close, but its June 26 low allows a fall of about 32%. Without his snapshot time this cannot be settled.

reviews.rationale: Nvidia (over 8%) and Microsoft (10%) hold. Oracle is roughly consistent. CoreWeave is contradicted: down about 7–9% on any reasonable baseline, not 'a bit over 4%'. SoftBank holds only on a daily reading, and Cerebras depends on an unknown intraday snapshot.

attribution.note: Marcus's own critique of Noah Smith, written in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the scope to the specific chart and his 'shows… not' wording. The 'doesn't follow' part is an argumentative judgment; what the chart shows can be checked.

contract.note: Judging by what the chart contains is fair. Whether 'less and less likely' counts as a 'no bubble' conclusion is an interpretation the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: Smith's actual wording was 'less and less likely', which is softer than 'no bubble'. That partly undercuts Marcus's characterization, but the chart is not shown.
The underlying Exponential View report. It covers more than revenue, but does not identify the chart Smith shared.

reviews.rationale: The chart Smith shared was not recovered, so it cannot be checked whether it showed only revenue. Smith's softer wording slightly weakens Marcus's paraphrase but is not enough to contradict the core point. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence. The quoted Bloomberg-style tweet that follows is not part of this claim.

semantics.note: Faithful. It keeps 'increasingly', 'lost steam', the slight daily gain, 11.74% for the week, and the bonds.

contract.note: Using the previous week's last close as the baseline is an ordinary reading. A 5-day chart window starting at the June 22 open could produce about 11.74% at some point during June 26. The result for the weekly figure depends on which convention is used.

evidence.note: Down 17.17% for the week on closing prices, and down 14.38% even at the June 26 high. This is far from 11.74% under the contract's convention.
Up 0.15% at the June 26 close, which matches 'up slightly for the day'.
A dated secondary summary reports newly issued bonds already trading below their issue price.
A reproduction of FT reporting describes falling bond prices, wider spreads, and a valuation resting on AI. It is hosted on a third-party site, which limits its weight.

reviews.rationale: The slight daily rise, the weak bonds and the AI framing are all supported. The specific 11.74% weekly fall is contradicted under the contract's closing-price convention: the stock was down 17.17%, and at least 14.38% even at the session high. It could only match on a 5-day chart window that is not recorded.
